chunks: From him, from one of his companions, raising it (to the Imam), he said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three things are not eaten and they fatten, and three are eaten and they slim (the body), and two benefit from every thing and do not harm from anything, and two harm from every thing and do not benefit from anything.'

So as for those which are not eaten and fatten: wearing linen, perfume, and Noura (lime-wax); and as for those which are eaten and slim: dried meat, cheese, and spadix; and in another Hadith: the prairie herb and oil-cake; and the two which benefit from everything and do not harm: lukewarm water and pomegranate; and the two which harm from everything and do not benefit: dried meat and cheese.
I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you, you said here they slim, and you said here they harm.' So he said, 'Do you not know that slimming is from the harm?'

key_terms.يَهْزِلْنَ: They slim (make the body lose weight/lean)
key_terms.يُسْمِنَّ: They fatten (make the body gain weight)

ai.seo_question: What are the three foods that slim the body and the two that harm everything according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) categorizes foods and substances based on their effects on the body, distinguishing between those that are not eaten but fatten, those eaten that slim, and pairs that either universally benefit or universally harm. The narration highlights that slimming can be a form of harm, illustrating the nuanced understanding of health and consumption in Shia tradition. This classification reflects the Shia emphasis on *al-Ishtiba'* (moderation) and the holistic view of the body as an *amanah* (trust), where dietary choices are evaluated not just for physical utility but for their spiritual and physiological balance.

en.hubeali: From him, from one of our companions, raising it, said,

‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Three things which are nor eaten and these fatten, and three are eaten and these slim (the body), and two benefit from every things and do not harm from anything, and two harm from everything and do not benefit from anything.

So as for those which are not eaten and these fatten are the linen, and the perfume, and the Noura (Lime-wax); and as for those which are eaten and they slim (the body), so these are the dried meat, and the cheese, and the spadix’ – and in another Hadeeth: ‘The Prairie moon (a herb), and oil-cake; and the two which benefit from everything and do not harm from anything the luke-warm water and the pomegranate; and those two which harm from everything and do not benefit from everything, so it is the dried meat, and the cheese’.

I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! Then you<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘They slimmen (the body)’, and over here they are both harmful’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘But do you not know that the slimming is from the harmful?’
en.sarwar: 7. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from certain persons of his people in a marfu‘ manner who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Use of three things forms fat in one’s body, another three things cause weight loss. Two things benefit harmlessly and two things do all kinds of harm without any benefit.

The three that can cause fatness are use of linen, perfume and lime. The ones that can cause weight loss are eating dried meat, cheese and spadix (al-Tal’). In another Hadith it is meat of the back of the camel and residue of oil.’ The two that benefit without harm are warm water and pomegranate, and the two that harm without any benefit are dried meat and cheese.’
I then said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, ‘Are the ones that cause weight loss harmful?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘Have you not heard that losing weight is harmful?”’
